source.title: Refusal Localizes, the Damage Relocates: Safety Layers Under Few-Sample Fine-Tuning
source.authors: Jungseob Lee; D. Lee; Sugyeong Eo; Seongtae Hong; Seungyoon Lee; Heuiseok Lim

record.tranche_reason: Tests harmful fine-tuning and whether localized interventions preserve or restore refusal, using LoRA attacks, explicit-refusal scoring, layer freezing, activation patching, and weight-update truncation. These results use a different experimental setup and measures from the cited original studies.
record.gate_note: The study does not measure per-token KL, compliant-opening prefills, suffix or decoding bypasses, or benign-only fine-tuning refusal rates. Its layer-patching results concern depth rather than response-token positions or a small parameter/rank subset. Cited results from prior work are not recorded as findings here.
record.test_reason: The study runs harmful LoRA SFT (5–100 PKU-SafeRLHF examples) on six aligned checkpoints and reports coherent refusal and Llama-Guard unsafe rates. This directly measures V1 with a different recipe from the originals. It also tests whether removing the top singular directions of the harmful update restores refusal, and whether freezing a localized layer band preserves it, which bears on V5. It does not measure per-token KL, prefill, suffix or decoding bypasses, benign-only refusal rates, or deepening training.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. To add: the authors find surviving prompt separability is mostly a property of the pretrained representation. They also find layer freezing does help at low harmful fractions or doses, e.g. accidental contamination of about 5%, and recommend reporting the dose at which a defense fails alongside its working range.
record.recipe_differences: Uses harmful instruction-response LoRA SFT and refusal-rate evaluation, but with the study's own PKU-SafeRLHF attack data, AdvBench evaluation, coherence-gated explicit-refusal metric, six checkpoints, and adaptive defense evaluations; exact original recipe comparison is not stated. Also tests layer freezing and update-spectrum repairs.
record.method_sensitivity: Dose and checkpoint affect attack success and transition depth; freezing boundary moves the recovery transition; training length and adapted projections weaken top-two repair; update concentration affects repair success.

fits_no_version.finding: A frozen clean-model probe still separates harmful from benign prompts after attack, but never-aligned base checkpoints separate them nearly as well (0.907–0.944).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Post-attack prompt separability is mostly a pretrained-representation property, not retained alignment.

fits_no_version.finding: Lockstep clean-state patching restores refusal at a reproducible layer depth (0.47–0.81 of depth). Freezing up to that depth relocates the transition upward rather than blocking the attack.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal recovery localizes along layer depth, but the localized site is not a fixed defensible site under adaptive fine-tuning.

record.problems: The authors note that the full freeze-boundary ladder covers one checkpoint and the cross-checkpoint sweep uses one rung per checkpoint; cross-model claims rest on four lineages, dose never exceeds 100, and the attack uses one objective and harmful corpus. Adaptive weight-space attacks and the detector are evaluated on Llama-3.1-8B. Several effects are reported as seed ranges, and the random-direction control is not matched for removed energy.
record.rows_left_out: Did not add separate rows for Llama-Guard unsafe rates, probe threshold accuracy/recalibration, detector statistics, task utility, or benign-set over-refusal; these are not the primary refusal measures in the tested versions. Did not add further layer-freeze ladder, donor-state patching, or activation-ablation results because those localize layers or hidden-state effects rather than the listed token-position or parameter/rank claims. The text reports these in Tables 1–21 and Appendices B–K.

untested.parts: Doses above 100; attack objectives other than response-masked SFT; harmful corpora other than PKU-SafeRLHF; closed or API models.

Benign-only fine-tuning refusal or harmfulness rates. Benign adapters are trained (Table 20 f=0, 75 detector adapters), but their refusal is not reported; only an unquantified aside says style-only training lowers refusal.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models across response positions.
Prefilling a compliant opening, adversarial suffixes and decoding changes.

Whether a small set of weights or ranks in the unmodified aligned model carries safety. Repair tests concern the harmful update's spectrum; the freeze tests concern a broad layer band (18 of 32 layers).
Whether data or objective causes token-shallow safety.
Training that deepens safety beyond early tokens, and its durability.

missing.what: Attack non-landing at low doses: no successful attack on OLMo-2-13B at 5 or 10 examples; dashes for Tulu, OLMo-7B and Qwen at low doses; 18 lockstep runs excluded for post-attack refusal >0.20
Low-dose freeze and matched arms, e.g. Llama dose 5 freeze .91–.96 vs attack .00–.05; OLMo-7B freeze .95–.98; Tulu .21–.52; Qwen .33–.60
Published SPPFT bands on Llama-3-8B, Llama-2-7b, gemma-2b and Phi-3, and full-FT gradient masking, all leaving refusal 0.00–0.19
missing.locator: Table 1 lower blocks; Table 13; Appendix F

missing.what: Writable-layer arms: OLMo-7B and OLMo-13B keep refusal 0.33–0.96 with 1–2 writable layers; four bottom layers suffice to break refusal on all six checkpoints
Top-2 repair across AdvBench, HarmBench and StrongREJECT (0.940/0.813/0.818 vs compromised ~0.00)
Safe LoRA-style projection versus scale-matched shrinkage; matched shrinkage equals projection against adaptive attacks

record.verdict_notes: The headline V1 measure is pattern-based coherent refusal. The authors stress that refusal and Llama-Guard disagree on 9,653 of 91,090 generations. The record left out the Llama-Guard rates, but V1 concerns harmful compliance, so the Table 1 unsafe columns should be added as rows. R18 is too thin for a V2 verdict; no benign-only refusal rate is reported anywhere. The V5 links rest on the harmful update's spectrum and on layer-band freezes, not on intrinsic localization of safety in the unmodified model. The Appendix J reproduction of single-direction refusal ablation (0.92–0.99 to 0.02–0.06) concerns an activation direction, not weights, so it is not linked.

versions.untested_parts: No dose above 100 harmful examples; the freeze and low-dose results are checkpoint- and setting-specific.
The study does not report numeric refusal rates for benign-only fine-tuning or isolate the effect of benign data from harmful examples in mixed-data runs.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models and its distribution across response positions.
Compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, and decoding changes as refusal bypasses.
The study tests repair by truncating harmful-update singular directions, not whether safety in an unmodified model is intrinsically carried by a small set of weights or ranks.
Whether data or training objective causes safety to be shallow across response tokens.
Training intended to spread safety beyond early response tokens and tests of whether that training holds up.

relationships.condition: Unrestricted harmful LoRA SFT at dose 100 on six checkpoints; low doses where the attack lands; restricted-layer attacks; mixed adapters with ≥5 harmful examples
relationships.reason: Coherent refusal falls from 0.91–1.00 to 0.00–0.18 (R1–R6, R13–R17). It stays near zero even when layers [0,ℓ*] are frozen (R7–R12) and in mixed adapters (R19–R21, R23–R24). Llama-Guard unsafe rises to 0.84–0.98 unrestricted (Table 1, text).
relationships.display_finding: Coherent refusal fell from 0.91–1.00 to 0.00–0.18 and stayed near zero with layers 0 to ℓ* frozen and in mixed adapters. Llama-Guard unsafe rates reached 0.84–0.98 for unrestricted attacks.

source_check.condition: Unrestricted harmful LoRA SFT at dose 100 on six checkpoints; low doses where the attack lands; restricted-layer attacks; mixed adapters with ≥5 harmful examples
source_check.reason: The cited successful-attack rows show substantial refusal loss, corroborated by unsafe-content rates. The frozen five-harmful-example mixed condition is separately covered by l1.

relationships.condition: Very low doses (5–10 examples) on some checkpoints, and low harmful fractions under a layer freeze
relationships.reason: Text, not rows: the attack does not land on OLMo-2-13B at 5 or 10 examples (Table 7), nor on Tulu, OLMo-7B or Qwen at the lowest doses (Table 8 dashes). With [0,17] frozen, 5% harmful data leaves refusal at 0.74–0.92 (R22).
relationships.display_finding: The attack did not land on OLMo-2-13B at 5 or 10 examples, nor on Tulu, OLMo-7B or Qwen at the lowest doses. With layers 0–17 frozen, 5% harmful data left refusal at 0.74–0.92.

relationships.condition: Restricted (frozen-band) attacks scored by Llama-Guard rather than refusal pattern
relationships.reason: Text, not rows: under freezes refusal stays ≤0.06, but Llama-Guard unsafe drops (e.g. OLMo-13B .23–.63 vs .89–.95). Safe non-refusals rise from 7% to 30%, so refusal loss overstates harmful compliance (R8–R11 context).
relationships.display_finding: Under freezes refusal stayed at or below 0.06, but Llama-Guard unsafe rates dropped (OLMo-13B 0.23–0.63 versus 0.89–0.95) and safe non-refusals rose from 7% to 30%, so refusal loss overstated harmful compliance.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Restricted (frozen-band) attacks scored by Llama-Guard rather than refusal pattern
source_check.reason: Table 1 and Section 5.1 show that near-zero explicit refusal can coexist with substantially reduced unsafe-content rates and safe non-refusals.

relationships.condition: Top-two singular-direction removal after short attention-only fine-tunes on four checkpoints, and after the projected adaptive attack on Llama
relationships.reason: Removing the update's top-2 directions restores refusal to 0.76–1.00 (R25–R28) and to 0.85 at one epoch (R29). Random-2 removal stays ≤0.26 (R37–R40, not energy-matched). The projected attack still allows 0.72–0.94 repair (R36).
relationships.display_finding: Removing the update's top two directions restored refusal to 0.76–1.00, and to 0.85 at one epoch, while removing two random directions, not energy-matched, left it at or below 0.26. Under the projected adaptive attack, repair still reached 0.72–0.94.

source_check.reason: R35 establishes failure of removing the top two harmful-update directions. V5 does not specify those two directions; this experiment does not establish absence of another small safety-carrying parameter or rank set.
